sections.h2: What does the Rowan County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
It keeps the official land records for Rowan County and records deeds, deeds of trust and maps. North Carolina register of deeds offices are elected county offices, and state law has the register collect the uniform recording fees and the excise tax on deeds before an instrument is recorded.

The county runs an online document search site for land records, and the office also takes vital record requests online. Property Check, a free alert service, is one more local tool for owners. Questions about Property Check go to 704-216-8636.

sections.h2: How does Property Check protect a Rowan County owner?
sections.html:
It sends an alert whenever a filing is recorded against a name or parcel number you register. Rowan County explains that the register does not judge whether a document is valid, so a fraudulent document that meets statutory recording rules and has the fees paid can still enter the public record.

The service is free and open around the clock, and you choose how to be notified. The county is frank that the alert does not stop fraud, but it lets you act quickly. If you suspect fraud, contact local law enforcement. Owners who hold inherited or vacant houses in Rowan County are the ones who gain most, because nobody is watching the record.

sections.h2: How do I record a map or plat in Rowan County?
sections.html:
Maps must be signed by the Rowan County Review Officer before they reach the register. The county accepts three sizes: 18 by 24 inches, 21 by 30 inches and 24 by 36 inches. Review Officers are at the Planning Office and the Tax Assessor's office on the second floor at 402 N Main Street in Salisbury.

When you record a map, you get the original back and the office keeps a digital copy. If your lot is in a recorded subdivision or you have a recorded survey, you can buy a copy for $2 from the register. The office also invites questions about recording maps electronically.

sections.h2: What recording fees and transfer tax does North Carolina set?
sections.html:
The statutes fix the fees statewide, so Rowan County charges the same as other counties. The grantor pays the excise tax before the deed is recorded.

Statewide amounts collected by the Rowan County register
ItemAmount in the statute
General instrument$26.00 for the first 15 pages, plus $4.00 per added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for the first 35 pages, plus $4.00 per added page
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, plus $2.00 per added page
Satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgageNo fee
Excise tax$1.00 per $500 or fractional part of consideration or value

Half of the excise tax goes to the county general fund, and the other half goes to the Department of Revenue, with the county allowed to keep 2% of the state share. A parcel in two counties is taxed in the county with the greater value.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter on a Rowan County sale?
sections.html:
Because a deed, option, lease over three years or similar instrument is not valid against lien creditors or buyers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the time of registration.

That is why a closing attorney will not release funds until the title is clear and the deed is ready to record. If you are selling a Rowan County house, ask the attorney to confirm that earlier mortgages were satisfied and that any heirship or divorce transfer is in the record.

sections.h2: What should a Rowan County seller check before listing?
sections.html:
Look at the recorded chain of title, then fix gaps. A seller can use the register's online search to see the last deed, any deed of trust and any liens, and a title company will do a full search. Common problems include a satisfied loan whose release was never recorded, a deed from a deceased owner and an old easement.

  • Pull the vesting deed and check that the name matches the person signing.
  • Look for any deed of trust without a recorded satisfaction. Satisfactions carry no recording fee.
  • Sign up for Property Check to watch for new filings while the house is vacant.
  • Ask the register's office how it wants a deed presented, since the office, not the statute, runs the counter day to day.

Selling to a cash buyer does not change the recording steps, because the deed is still presented to the register in the county where the property sits.

faqs.q: Does Rowan County offer online land record search?
faqs.a: Yes. The county links an online document search site for land records, and Property Check uses the same system to alert owners about new filings.
It is free. You create an account, register a name or parcel number and choose how to be notified when a document is recorded.

faqs.q: What map sizes can be recorded in Rowan County?
faqs.a: The accepted sizes are 18 by 24, 21 by 30 and 24 by 36 inches, and the Review Officer must sign the map first.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Rowan County?
faqs.a: The transferor, meaning the seller, pays it to the register before recording at $1.00 per $500 or fractional part of the price.

faqs.q: How much is a copy of a recorded survey?
faqs.a: The county says a copy of a recorded subdivision map or survey costs $2 at the Register of Deeds.
